impact.rationale: The production change is in the recovery-store draft-copy path immediately before preparation and publication of persistent recovery state; an error can reject a legitimate recovery transition or construct state different from the validated raw authority.

regressionLikelihood.rationale: Ordinary canonical equality and raw-mismatch fallback are supported, but a concrete coordinated private typed mutation reaches a new marshal-error rejection that the prior raw-only copy accepts. The precondition is narrow, but this repository explicitly tests coordinated private mutation as a consistency boundary.

regressionProtection.rationale: Existing and added source tests cover ordinary equality, byte mismatch, detachment, nil/empty/capacity, representation, ownership, generation, disk and CAS boundaries, but omit clone-success plus json.Marshal failure; no exact-candidate Go/gofmt/Linux check ran.

recoverability.rationale: The unintegrated candidate changes no persisted schema, migration, dependency or runtime switch; revising or omitting it preserves the old path, and a two-file revert would restore it if integrated.

confidence.rationale: The immutable patch and supplied hashes were independently bound; changed symbols, callers, clone graph and source/FMT/name closure were statically traced. Runtime acceptance remains intentionally unclaimed.

applicability.rationale: copyRecord is used by owned internal/mihomodeploy recovery begin/revoke and candidate-preparation paths, so the production delta is live rather than test-only.

statusQuoRisk.rationale: The old raw-only copy is behaviorally safe and the candidate claims no measured performance benefit; no paired same-flags Linux measurement establishes the cost of retaining it.

riskDrivers: Confirmed new rejection when a valid issued base has a cloneable typed image that cannot be JSON-marshaled while its bound raw bytes remain valid.
The path feeds persistent lifecycle recovery preparation and publication.
No exact-candidate Go, gofmt, ordinary, race or Linux execution evidence exists.
protectiveFactors: Existing ownership, active-base, poison, raw digest, raw byte, typed equality and one-use gates are unchanged.
Byte mismatch falls back to lifecycleTrustedJSONCopy of the bound raw authority.
The closed clone allocates pointer/slice/byte storage and preserves nil versus empty with current schema coverage.
No public capability, callback, environment switch, schema change, migration, dependency or prefix cache is added.
Both changed files are in normal source/gofmt declarations and the unchanged workflow pins 688 top-level names.

materialBoundaries.invariant: After verified-base validity gates pass, copyRecord must return the same detached record as decoding bound raw bytes, including coordinated private typed-image changes.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: Set both store and base LastTrustedAt after issuance to time.Date(10000,1,1,0,0,0,0,time.UTC). b.valid remains true and cloneTrustedLifecycleV3 succeeds because the value is UTC without monotonic data; json.Marshal then fails for the out-of-range year. The old implementation decodes unchanged valid raw, while the candidate returns errLifecycleUnsafe.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Because raw already passed custody, digest, exact-byte and prior canonical/semantic validation, both json.Marshal error and byte inequality can safely fall back to lifecycleTrustedJSONCopy(b.core.raw), restoring the old result.

materialBoundaries.invariant: The optimization must not bypass ownership, active-base, poison, used-base, disk custody, generation, preparation, CAS or publication checks.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A foreign store, spent base, changed validation generation, or disk image changed after copy attempts publication.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: b.valid/issuedTo, validated binding, disk reread, base.used, prepare and publish checks remain outside and unchanged; added subtests target those rejection sites.

materialBoundaries.invariant: The draft must not share mutable pointers, slices, bytes, aliases, spare capacity, nil/empty distinctions or RawMessage storage with store/base.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: Mutating returned ControlBytes, capabilities, sibling pointers or hidden slice capacity changes the trusted source graph.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Closed clone helpers allocate per pointer/slice path and copy bytes; schema excludes maps/interfaces/functions; existing properties cover 63 structs, 86 mutable slots, aliases and representation fallbacks.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Both changed files remain in normal source, gofmt and unchanged required top-name contracts.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A changed file is omitted from source/FMT, or added top-level tests silently change the 688-name set.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Static inspection found both paths in normal gofmt/source declarations, the test in TEST_FILES, and workflow pins count 688 plus b0a464294a9dcaf7bea46ea29c0e7bc4937acc63b16df05387d3652efbbcb280; new cases are subtests.
